verdicts.reason: All quotes verified verbatim: 24.01.01-report-intake-notice-and-action.md:36-38 ('Three reason families **bypass the general moderation queue entirely** ... factual rights disputes (→ domains 02/09, not a policy question)'), 24.01-reporting-moderation-cx.md:26-27 (same), 24.01.03-moderation-queue-reviewer-ops.md:39 ('the music-domain queues (sample clearance, credit disputes, gear authenticity, mix-ownership)'), :52 ('S2 | Standard policy violation or factual dispute | Skill-routed by reason family') and :81 ('all others select a skill-scoped queue (e.g. `sample-clearance`, `credit-dispute`, ...)'). The domain CX is not a third position — trust-safety-disputes-cx.md:209-211 and, decisively, :427 ('It is **not** general-queue load — it never enters the moderation queue, so CX-06's carve-out holds') answer where the adjudication work lives (the shared `Dispute Case Engine`, 02.05) and its SLA ownership. That collapses most of the claimed forced invention. What survives is a genuine unmarked contradiction: 24.01.03 enumerates `credit-dispute` / 'credit disputes' among its OWN skill-scoped queues and classes 'factual dispute' as S2 inside this queue, while 24.01.01:36-38, cx:26-27 and domain cx:427 say those cases never enter it. Two implementers do diverge on queue topology (a credit-dispute lane inside 24.01.03 vs ejection at intake). Downgraded from blocking to warning because the reconciliation direction is stated normatively at trust-safety-disputes-cx.md:427 — the defect is a stale queue enumeration in 24.01.03, not absent product behaviour.

Both quotes exist (24.01.01:60-61 'dedups against existing open cases on the same target + reason within a rolling 30-day window'; 24.01-reporting-moderation-cx.md:36-37 'Merge strategy: dedup by (target, reason-family)'), but there is no contradiction to resolve. The CX file is the unit that owns merge strategy and states it explicitly and normatively as (target, reason-family); the feature file's happy-path bullet says 'target + reason' as loose shorthand in a numbered step, in a file that elsewhere speaks of 'reason families' (24.01.01:36). Nothing in 24.01.01 asserts code-level granularity, and the behaviour that depends on dedup — the brigading case at 24.01.01:72 ('Dedups to one case with 400 reporter references') and the invariant at :50-51 ('Volume dedups; it does not escalate') — is unaffected by the granularity either way. Detail carried one file over is not missing detail.

Quotes verified (trust-safety-disputes-cx.md:284-286, :295-297; 24.02.05:33-35 and D-02 at :104; 24.05.03:28-30 and :64), but every reasonable reading converges on one build. CX-09's operative 'Trigger chain' two lines below the loose relationship sentence is unambiguous — cx:295 'listing submit → both checks run → refusals merged into one message' — and cx:297 'both are **pre-publication** gates'. Both children agree that listing is the moment both engines evaluate: 24.02.05:33-35 runs at listing AND at checkout/shipping (destination test), 24.05.03:29 detects 'at listing time'. The merged refusal therefore lands at listing submit, which is the only moment at which both engines have an opinion; 24.02.05's second, checkout-time pass is a destination/shippability test that 24.05.03 has no counterpart for, so there is nothing to merge there and nothing to invent. The 'unable to evaluate' branch is also specified, not open: cx:296 'A rebuild failure keeps the old projection and alerts — never fail open (E-12)' and 24.02.05:67 'Fail closed'. The single phrase 'at checkout' in cx:286 is a drafting slip contradicted by its own section and both children.

The quote at 24.09-case-evidence-locker.md:144 is verbatim and its 'What User Sees' cell is indeed loosely worded, but the behaviour it garbles is fully and normatively specified 60 lines above in the same file: :78-81 'A **GDPR erasure request** against a bundle still inside another clock's window resolves to **anonymise-and-retain, not a blanket hard-delete of the whole bundle** ... PII fields are tombstoned, financial and evidentiary records are kept', restated as D-06 at :184 'Retention = max of applicable clocks; legal hold = infinity; erasure = anonymise-and-retain'. The state a partially-anonymised bundle occupies is likewise derivable without invention: :143 'Retained | Case closed, no hold, clocks running'. An implementer builds erasure as a tombstoning operation on a Retained bundle and purge as the max-of-clocks delete (:74, :147-148) — no divergence. The defect is a redundant restatement in one table cell, not a missing rule.

The facts check out — trust-safety-disputes-index.md:70-78 shows `[SURFACE]` in the Status column for 24.01–24.09, while all eight sub-domain indexes carry '> **Status**: [BREADTH]' at line 5 and 24.09-case-evidence-locker.md:5 carries '[DEEP]' — but the claimed gating ambiguity does not exist. The index's own header at trust-safety-disputes-index.md:5 reads '> **Status**: [BREADTH]', agreeing with its children, and the Children-table note at :65-66 is explicitly a dated snapshot ('Classified 2026-07-16 by `/ideate-discover` Step 3 ... All nodes `[SURFACE]`') rather than a current assertion. Every child file's own line-5 header is unambiguous and, as the finding itself concedes, the sub-domain indexes' Children tables all match their features exactly — so the tree's convention that a node's own header is authoritative is established by uniform practice. No pipeline decision turns on the stale column, and no implementer invents behaviour from it. Low-value hygiene, not an ambiguity.

All three quotes verified verbatim (24.02.05:67 and D-03 at :105 'The only feature in domain 24 where failing closed is correct'; 24.08.01:72 'the only other place in domain 24 that fails closed is 24.02.05'; 24.03.05:60 'Fail closed on payouts' and D-03 at :99). The uniqueness clauses are rationale prose attached to an edge-case row and a decision-context column, not behavioural specifications, and every affected feature states its own posture in its own file as a first-class decision: 24.02.05 D-03, 24.08.01:72, 24.03.05 D-03. Nobody building 24.03.05 reads 24.02.05's rationale and makes sanctions screening fail open — 24.03.05:60 tells them exactly what to do and why ('Delaying money is recoverable; paying a sanctioned party is not'). The claimed forced invention, a 'domain-wide default availability posture', is not a thing any of these features consumes; posture is specified per feature (e.g. 24.03.01:56 'Fail open with rules aware they are blind'). Every reasonable reading converges on the same build.

The States table at 24.02.01-enforcement-ladder-sanctions.md:135-142 does lack a row naming rung 8, but each item of the claimed forced invention is answered in the same file. The sanction record is generic — :34 'A sanction is a record `(subject, act, rule-version-pinned, scope, severity, duration, reversibility, ...)`' — so rung 8 carries a duration like every other rung, with :39 'Duration is explicit; `indefinite` is a distinct, higher-severity value' and :108 'The sanction expires automatically on its `duration` end timestamp, or is reversed on appeal (24.02.02) with a restoration cascade (CX-03)', which places rung 8 squarely in Expired/Reversed. Expiry-vs-terminal is settled by :54's own Reversible column, 'Fully for the entity; must not touch co-owners' — not terminal like rung 7. Concurrence and the Proposed state are covered by :103 and D-07 at :178, whose context column names 'entity action' explicitly as a rung ≥ 6 case. Scope is a mandatory field with `entity` in its containment order (D-04 at :175), and the user-visible effect is spelled out at :73-76. What is left is a missing label in one table, i.e. downstream data-model naming, not product behaviour.

Quotes verified (24.02.03:13-14, :67-68; 24.02.02:27, :37-39, D-01 at :96, Q-02 at :105). The premise that the appeal surface may simply not exist is itself contingent on a question that is tracked with a named owner and a named target: 24.02.02:105 'Q-02 | Confirm the Art 19 carve-out with counsel before treating the appeal surface as Should rather than Must. | User + counsel | `/create-prd-security`', corroborated by 24.02.03:143 Q-01 and 24.02-enforcement-appeals-policy-index.md:66 Q-01 (same owner and target). That is the documented mechanism for a not-yet-due legal determination, and the tracking is well-formed. Note also what the question actually asks — 'Should rather than Must', i.e. a MoSCoW demotion, not deletion — and that 24.02.02 is specified in full with D-01 at :96 keeping reversibility ungated, so the redress route's target is built either way. 24.02.03:68 additionally names the alternative pointer ('and, where applicable, the out-of-court settlement pointer'). The auditor's demanded sub-question is downstream of a counsel answer that is already owned.

The quote at 24.03.01-risk-scoring-rules-engine.md:105 is verbatim and is the textbook refutation case: it is a well-formed deferral carrying both an owner and a target — '| Q-03 | What is an acceptable false-positive rate on a payout hold ... | User | `/create-prd-compile` |' — explicitly re-targeted to the stage that owns engineering budgets and thresholds. The claim that the unit then has 'no testable acceptance criterion of any kind' is also overstated on its own quoted evidence: 24.03.01:53 'Multi-hyphenate performs 5 unrelated role-actions in an hour | **Must not flag.**', :54 'Shared-IP linkage must not fire', :55 'Step-up verification, not a block', :58 'must be structurally impossible' and :59 'The label must flow back as a **negative** label' are all binary, testable assertions. Suppressing threshold values is a deliberate, sourced decision (24.03-fraud-risk-operations-index.md:41-42), and the numeric operating point is owned elsewhere — not missing.

Both quotes verified (24.04.03-buyer-seller-protection-programs.md:57 '`[PENDING]` — see Q-02'; Q-02 at :112 struck through and '**Resolved**: escrow with milestone release, with the platform's own session record as the fact base ... homed in the Payments, Escrow & Payouts cross-cut, not in this programme'), and the finding's own forcedInvention field concedes 'Nothing — the answer exists'. A struck-through question annotated **Resolved**, with its source cited (this file's D-03 at :105, 'Services are out of scope for this programme ... They need escrow with milestone release'), unambiguously supersedes the pointer that references it; no competent reader treats a resolved question as an open one, and the marker is in the 'User Sees' column of one edge-case row 55 lines above its own resolution in the same file. Stale cross-reference, zero build divergence.

The marker at 24.04.03:61 ('Counterfeit discovered a year later (a refin sold as original) ... `[PENDING]` — the vintage market's defining timing problem') is verbatim and is indeed bare, but the identical scenario is specified with behaviour AND a well-formed deferral in the sibling unit that owns authenticity: 24.05.03-authenticity-counterfeit-brand-protection.md:61 '| Discovered two years later | Every standard window (returns, protection, chargeback, claim) has closed ... a **long-tail authenticity flag** attaches to the registry record and the misrepresentation is recorded against the original seller's history even where no monetary remedy remains. Whether a **monetary** remedy exists past the window is `[PENDING — /create-prd]` (Q-02, DT-03) | "Reported outside the guarantee window — recorded on the item's registry history" |', with 24.05.03:112 'Q-02 | **[OWNER]** ... | User | `/create-prd`'. Both halves of the auditor's forced invention — what the parties are told, and which stage decides the monetary remedy — are therefore answered and owned one file over. 24.05.03:41 makes the cross-unit ownership explicit ('Authenticity failures also surface **years late**, which breaks the claim windows every other feature in [domain 24 relies on]').

Quotes verified (24.04.01-claims-dispute-filing.md:34-36, :41, :65, :72; 24.04.02:59's 5-day mediation default). But the vision layer specifies the behaviour completely: the window is an inherited attribute of the bound transaction object (:41, and D-01 per 24.04.01:106 'the remedy set is an attribute of the bound object'), it gates the Available state and terminates in Expired with 'No claim route' (:65, :72). What is absent is only the numeric value per object type — and :34-36 names its two governing sources rather than leaving them open: 'constrained by statutory returns rights (the Tax/consumer-protection cross-cut) and by the card networks' own clocks (24.04.04)'. Those are legal facts and engineering budget values of exactly the class this tree consistently routes downstream (24.01.03:45-46 defers per-tier SLA values to `/create-prd-security`; 24.09:193 Q-03 defers statutory clock values to counsel). The comparison to 24.04.02:59's 5-day mediation default does not carry — that window is a pure platform choice with no statutory or card-network constraint, so it can be fixed at the vision layer while the filing windows cannot.

Every quote checks out (24.07.02:61, 24.07.03:59, 24.07.02:71, 24.07.03:76, cx:75-77), but the governing rule for the scenario is ratified in the sub-domain's own index: 24.07-identity-abuse-ownership-disputes-index.md:65 — 'Q-01 | ~~**Should the platform adjudicate who owns a band name at all?**~~ **RESOLVED — no. The platform executes a *recorded* disposition rule against its own state and never adjudicates a claim; where nothing was recorded, or the claim is contested, it freezes and routes out.**', restated at 24.07.02:106. That rule is claim-class-agnostic and answers the finding's forced invention directly: neither claim class takes precedence, because the platform decides neither — a contested claim with no recorded disposition freezes and routes out. The resulting state is already in the machine: 24.07.02:72 '| Frozen indefinitely | Legal proceedings elsewhere | The account persists, earns, and does nothing else |', with the freeze semantics fixed at :68 (consequential actions frozen, accruals unaffected), :59 (export included in the freeze) and cx:68-70 (accruals must continue). An implementer building the estate-vs-ownership race under the ratified rule reaches one answer. What is genuinely defective here is the staleness of the `[PENDING]` markers relative to that resolution — which is finding #014, upheld separately; scoring it twice would double-count.

Verified item by item against the files. Stale pointers to resolved questions: 24.07.02:55 and :71 both defer to '24.07 Q-01', which 24.07-identity-abuse-ownership-disputes-index.md:65 and 24.07.02:106 record as '**RESOLVED — freeze and route**'; 24.07.03:64 defers to 'Q-02', resolved at 24.07.03:110 ('**RESOLVED — yes, as two separate capabilities over one party**'); 24.07.03:58 carries '`[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]`' — a completed stage — while :111 records the same question as '**RESOLVED — they never join**'. Malformed markers with neither owner nor target: 24.07.02:61, 24.07.03:59, 24.07.03:76. 24.07.03:57 names a domain ('domain 01's model must anticipate this') rather than an owner or a stage. The count holds: 24.07.03's Open Questions at :109-111 are all three struck through and resolved, while five behaviours (:57, :58, :59, :64, :76) remain marked PENDING. Under the deferral rule this is the exception that survives — the tracking itself is malformed or stale, not merely not-yet-due. Held at warning, not blocking: the substantive answers exist (the ratified freeze-and-route rule at index:65, the resolved Q-02/Q-03 in 24.07.03), so no implementer must invent product behaviour; the defect is that the markers point at answers already given, which will mislead the next stage into re-opening settled decisions.
